prompt: The five aromatic ring protons of toluene (methylbenzene) give one complex, overlapping pattern in its ^1H NMR spectrum. Why?

choices.text: Their signals overlap by accident, even though they aren't all equivalent
All five ring protons are equivalent
choices.why: They aren't all equivalent; the pattern is complex because their nonequivalent signals happen to overlap.

choices.text: The methyl signal lies on top of them
choices.why: The methyl protons absorb well upfield of the aromatic protons.

choices.text: Aromatic protons can't couple with one another
choices.why: The complexity comes from accidental overlap of nonequivalent signals, not from a lack of coupling.

explanation: Different kinds of hydrogens often have accidentally overlapping signals. In toluene, the five aromatic ring protons give a complex, overlapping pattern, even though they aren't all equivalent (Figure 13.8.1).

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring), what splitting pattern does the aldehyde proton at 9.69 δ show?

choices.text: A doublet, split by the proton on carbon 2
A singlet, because the aldehyde proton has no neighbors
choices.why: The proton on carbon 2 is its neighbor and splits its signal.

choices.text: A triplet, split by the protons on carbons 2 and 3
choices.why: Only the carbon 2 proton is adjacent to the aldehyde proton, so the signal is a doublet.

choices.text: A doublet of doublets, split by the protons on carbons 2 and 3
choices.why: The carbon 2 proton is the one with two different neighbors. The aldehyde proton has just one.

explanation: The aldehyde proton at carbon 1 appears in the normal downfield position at 9.69 δ and is split into a doublet, with J = 6 Hz, by the adjacent proton at carbon 2.

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring), what is the coupling constant of the aldehyde proton's doublet, in Hz?
explanation: The aldehyde proton at 9.69 δ is split into a doublet with J = 6 Hz by the adjacent proton on carbon 2.

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring), the proton on carbon 2 is coupled to the aldehyde proton (J = 6 Hz) and to the proton on carbon 3 (J = 12 Hz). How many lines does its signal show?
explanation: Coupling with the carbon 3 proton splits the signal into a doublet (J = 12 Hz). Coupling with the aldehyde proton splits each of those lines into a doublet (J = 6 Hz). That gives four lines, a doublet of doublets, at 6.73 δ.

prompt: A proton is coupled to two nonequivalent neighboring protons with two different coupling constants, giving four lines. What is this pattern called?

choices.text: A doublet of doublets
A quartet
choices.why: A quartet comes from three equivalent neighbors, with one J and 1 : 3 : 3 : 1 intensities.

choices.text: A doublet of triplets
choices.why: Triplets would need two equivalent neighbors with the same J. Here each neighbor gives its own doublet.

choices.text: A quintet
choices.why: A quintet has five lines and comes from four equivalent neighbors.

explanation: The carbon 2 proton of trans-cinnamaldehyde is split into a doublet by one neighbor, and each line is split again into a doublet by the other neighbor. The four-line result is a doublet of doublets (Figure 13.8.2).

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring), the vinylic proton on carbon 3 absorbs at 7.49 δ, downfield of the normal vinylic region. Why?

choices.text: It is next to the aromatic ring
It is bonded to an oxygen atom
choices.why: Carbon 3 isn't bonded to oxygen. It is bonded to the aromatic ring.

choices.text: Its signal is split into a doublet
choices.why: Splitting divides a signal into lines; it doesn't move the signal downfield.

choices.text: It is coupled to the aldehyde proton
choices.why: The carbon 3 proton is coupled only to the carbon 2 proton. Its downfield shift comes from the nearby ring.

explanation: The vinylic proton at carbon 3 is next to the aromatic ring and is therefore shifted downfield from the normal vinylic region, to 7.49 δ.

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring), the carbon 2 proton couples to the carbon 3 proton with J = 12 Hz. What coupling constant does the carbon 3 proton's doublet show, in Hz?
explanation: Two protons coupled to each other share the same coupling constant. The carbon 3 proton has one neighbor, the carbon 2 proton, so its signal is a doublet with J = 12 Hz.

prompt: How does a tree diagram build up the signal of the carbon 2 proton in trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring)?

choices.text: A 12 Hz doublet from the carbon 3 proton, then each line split into a 6 Hz doublet by the aldehyde proton
A 12 Hz doublet from the carbon 3 proton, then each line split into a 6 Hz triplet by the aldehyde proton
choices.why: There is only one aldehyde proton, so it splits each line into a doublet, not a triplet.

choices.text: A 6 Hz doublet from the carbon 3 proton, then each line split into a 12 Hz doublet by the aldehyde proton
choices.why: The coupling constants are swapped. The carbon 2–carbon 3 coupling is 12 Hz and the aldehyde coupling is 6 Hz.

choices.text: A single 9 Hz triplet from both neighbors together
choices.why: The n + 1 rule works only for equivalent neighbors with the same J. These two neighbors have different J values.

explanation: A tree diagram shows the effect of each coupling in turn. Coupling with the carbon 3 proton splits the carbon 2 signal into a doublet with J = 12 Hz; coupling with the aldehyde proton then splits each peak into a doublet with J = 6 Hz, giving four lines (Figure 13.8.3).

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, C6H5CH=CHCHO (carbon 1 is the aldehyde carbon; carbon 3 is bonded to the ring), the carbon 2 proton is split by the carbon 3 proton (J = 12 Hz) and by the aldehyde proton (J = 6 Hz). How far apart, in Hz, are the two outermost lines of its four-line signal?
explanation: The 12 Hz splitting puts two lines 6 Hz on either side of the center. Each is split again by 6 Hz, into lines 3 Hz on either side. The four lines sit at −9, −3, +3 and +9 Hz from the center, so the outer two are 18 Hz (12 + 6) apart.

prompt: The four peaks of the carbon 2 proton signal in trans-cinnamaldehyde are not all the same size. Why?

choices.text: When coupled protons have similar chemical shifts, peaks nearer the partner's signal are larger
When coupled protons have similar chemical shifts, peaks farther from the partner's signal are larger
choices.why: It's the reverse: the peaks nearer the coupled partner are always the larger ones.

choices.text: The four peaks come from different numbers of protons
choices.why: All four peaks come from the same single proton on carbon 2.

choices.text: Peaks at higher field are always weaker
choices.why: The size difference depends on where the coupled partner absorbs, not on the field itself.

explanation: A size difference occurs whenever coupled nuclei have similar chemical shifts, here 7.49 δ for the carbon 3 proton and 6.73 δ for the carbon 2 proton. The peaks nearer the signal of the coupled partner are always larger.

prompt: In trans-cinnamaldehyde, the carbon 2 proton absorbs at 6.73 δ and its coupled partner, the carbon 3 proton, at 7.49 δ. Which peaks of the carbon 2 multiplet are larger?

choices.text: The two left-hand peaks, nearer the 7.49 δ signal
The two right-hand peaks, farther from the 7.49 δ signal
choices.why: The peaks nearer the coupled partner are the larger ones. 7.49 δ lies to the left of 6.73 δ.

choices.text: The two middle peaks
choices.why: The skewing runs toward the partner's signal, so the left-hand pair is larger.

choices.text: None; all four are the same size
choices.why: Because the two coupled protons have similar shifts, the multiplet is skewed toward its partner.

explanation: Downfield is to the left, so the 7.49 δ signal lies to the left of 6.73 δ. The left-hand peaks of the carbon 2 multiplet, nearer the carbon 3 absorption, are larger than the right-hand peaks.

prompt: How can the skewing of a multiplet help you interpret a ^1H NMR spectrum?

choices.text: It shows where to find the coupled partner: look in the direction of the larger peaks
It shows where to find the coupled partner: look in the direction of the smaller peaks
choices.why: The larger peaks are the ones nearer the coupled partner, so look toward them.

choices.text: It gives the number of protons causing the signal
choices.why: The number of protons comes from integration, not from skewing.

choices.text: It gives the coupling constant directly
choices.why: The coupling constant is the spacing between peaks, not their relative sizes.

explanation: The skewing effect on multiplets tells where to look in the spectrum to find the coupled partner: look in the direction of the larger peaks.

prompt: Splitting of one proton by which kind of neighbors does the n + 1 rule predict?

choices.text: Equivalent neighboring protons
Nonequivalent neighboring protons with different coupling constants
choices.why: Splitting by nonequivalent protons is more complex, like the doublet of doublets of trans-cinnamaldehyde's carbon 2 proton.

choices.text: Any magnetic nuclei, however far away
choices.why: Protons farther than two carbons apart don't usually couple.

choices.text: Only protons on the same carbon
choices.why: Equivalent protons on the same carbon don't split each other. The rule counts protons on neighboring carbons.

explanation: The n + 1 rule predicts splitting caused by equivalent protons. Splittings caused by nonequivalent protons are more complex and are best worked out with a tree diagram.

prompt: In 3-bromo-1-phenyl-1-propene, C6H5CH=CHCH2Br, the vinylic proton on carbon 2 is coupled to the vinylic proton on carbon 1 (J = 16 Hz) and to the two methylene protons on carbon 3 (J = 8 Hz). How many lines does its signal show?
explanation: The 16 Hz coupling gives a doublet with lines 8 Hz either side of center. The two carbon 3 protons split each line into an 8 Hz triplet, giving lines at −16, −8, 0 and 0, +8, +16 Hz. The two lines at 0 coincide, so five lines are seen (Exercise 13.8.1).

prompt: In 3-bromo-1-phenyl-1-propene, C6H5CH=CHCH2Br, the carbon 2 proton is split into a 16 Hz doublet by the carbon 1 proton, and each line into an 8 Hz triplet by the two carbon 3 protons. Why are five lines seen rather than six?

choices.text: Because 16 Hz is exactly twice 8 Hz, an inner line of each triplet falls at the same position
The two carbon 3 protons are nonequivalent, so one splitting is lost
choices.why: The two carbon 3 protons are equivalent and together give a triplet. The missing line comes from two lines landing in the same place.

choices.text: One line is too small to see
choices.why: No line is missing; two of the six lines coincide and add together at the center.

choices.text: The carbon 2 proton has four equivalent neighbors, so the n + 1 rule gives five lines
choices.why: It has three neighbors, and they aren't all equivalent: one on carbon 1 (16 Hz) and two on carbon 3 (8 Hz).

explanation: The doublet lines sit 8 Hz either side of center. Splitting each into an 8 Hz triplet puts one triplet at 0, +8, +16 Hz and the other at −16, −8, 0 Hz. The two lines at 0 overlap, so a five-line multiplet is observed (Exercise 13.8.1).
